page: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores utilizing the Intel Xeon 8124M processor with an x86_64 architecture. The dedicated CPU cores operate at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz and include 24 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.67 GB of memory per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type, meaning storage requirements must be met via network-attached volumes.

In benchmark evaluations, the c5n.18xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 66660.83 and a Passmark CPU score of 49891.05. Its memory subsystem shows strong capabilities, achieving a read-only large block bandwidth of 208.32 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 90.55 GB/sec. Database operations are also highly rated, with Passmark database operations scoring 22220.88 and Redis SET operations reaching 61.1 million operations per second. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier, and LLM text generation speeds are weak, yielding 7.23 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

This instance is designed with a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, making it suitable for network-bound workloads. Given the high vCPU count, strong multi-core processing, and high network throughput, the c5n.18xlarge is suited for high-performance computing, distributed analytics, network appliances, and database operations that rely on network-attached storage. The lack of local storage and GPU accelerators makes it less suitable for local-disk-intensive databases or large-scale deep learning training.
